parsed_response.rubric_rationale: An evidence-sufficiency benchmark should accept unknown grounded in at least one applicable, unresolved issue that independently prevents establishing complete-product suitability. Here, incomplete composition of explicitly excluded trimmings suffices in both cases. Exhaustive issue enumeration is a separate reporting-completeness criterion; it should not be required to recognize a correctly grounded conservative unknown. Unsupported unknowns and issues drawn solely from unrelated candidates should fail. Positive findings and definite animal allegations still require strict target identity and exact source applicability, including relevant variant, market and period limitations. Catalogue associations and capture dates cannot supply that proof. Neither retained candidate mismatches nor a policy permitting animal materials establish animal content in these targets.
